attributeInstructions: Return call transcript analysis as the following JSON dictionary object. The current company will always be one of the following: TXU Energy, Ambit Energy, TriEagle Energy, Ambit, Txu, TriEagleTx, Dynegy, BetterBuy, EnergyHarbor, Crius, USGE, Veridian, Brighten, Homefield, PublicPower, TeepaNj, Universal4CHG, Residential4CHG, UniversalEXP, ResidentialEXP, UniversalVET, ResidentialVET – anything to the contrary is a transcription error and should be corrected into the one that best fits. TXU Energy, Ambit Energy, and TriEagle Energy will appear most frequently in transcripts, so choose whichever of these fits the context when ambiguous. Agents may refer to current company as a separate entity, so that is not exclusion criterion.

attributes.call_summary: Succinctly summarize the call's initial intent, primary intent (if different), actions taken by the agent, and conclusion in one sentence. Include as many specific details as possible, and format in a way that's easy for you to aggregate later. Must include following information if present in transcript: Lubbock, competitor offer, competitor name, customer filing complaint.
attributes.PUC_risk_reasoning: If customer said anything that would suggest an extremely high risk for PUC complaint against OUR company, limited to mentions of: PUC, Public Utilities Commission, BBB, Better Business Bureau, Austin, lawyers, news outlets or media, journalists, politicians, give a short summary of why here. Switching companies or generic dissatisfaction is not a risk factor. If there is no such threat, output exactly "" (an empty string) — do NOT write “none”, “no complaint”, “null”, “N/A”, or any other words.
attributes.taboo_reasoning: Provide a one or two-sentence reason for your evaluation of 'taboo_topics', if '1'. Give specific verbatim details where applicable. If no discussion of politics or controversial topics occurred, return blank.
attributes.taboo_topics: Indicate '1' or '0' whether the agent actively participated in a discussion of politics, taboo, or controversial issues. The agent must engage the customer beyond polite responses.
attributes.PUC_risk_verbatim:
If the output of PUC_risk_reasoning is "", return "".
Otherwise, return the exact verbatim quote from the customer’s transcript that warranted the PUC/BBB/legal/media escalation (no paraphrasing, no added words).
attributes.issue_unresolved: Indicate '1' or '0' whether the customer ended the call without some kind of resolution to their request(s), not evaluating whether the resolution was satisfactory.
attributes.agent_grammar_mistakes: First determine who is the TRUE agent in the transcript, not just who is labeled as such (use context). Then count how many times the agent makes frequent mistakes with English phrases, verb tenses, or basic grammar. Give some leeway to the fact that this is a spoken transcript, so exclude things like repeated words or incomplete sentences. Must be egregious and almost unintelligible to qualify.
attributes.insights_reasoning: Return two sections only, in this exact order, with these exact headings: 'Insight:' and 'Tags:'. Do not add any other headings or commentary. Insight: Write 2–4 sentences describing one primary, aggregation-worthy insight from the call. Sentence 1 must state the call outcome (sale, no_sale, service_only, or unknown) and the customer’s intent in a few words. Sentence 2–4 must explain the main driver of that outcome or the most unusual/high-friction/positive element of the interaction, prioritizing (when present) the reason for a no-sale or sale, policy/product confusion, process friction (holds, transfers, authentication, disconnects, system issues), competitor mentions, escalation risk, compliance concerns, customer delight, or a clear sentiment shift and what triggered it. Include at least one piece of concrete evidence: either a short verbatim quote of 12 words or fewer, or a specific detail such as a price, term length, fee, eligibility requirement, timing constraint, step that failed, great agent strategy, or policy statement. Remain neutral and factual: do not recommend actions, do not speculate, and do not infer motives. If a key detail is unclear due to transcript quality, explicitly state that it is unclear rather than guessing. Ignore obvious transcription errors and incorrect company names, but do not silently 'fix' numbers, dates, or commitments; if uncertain, mark unclear. Tags: Provide exactly one line in the following format with no extra text: Outcome=<sale|no_sale|service_only|unknown>; Intent=<1-3 words>; Driver=<1-3 words>; Topic=<1-3 words>; Sentiment=<positive|neutral|negative|mixed|unclear>; EvidenceType=<quote|detail|none>; Confidence=<high|med|low>. Use 'none' for EvidenceType only if the transcript contains no usable quote or concrete detail. Use Confidence=low when the transcript is fragmented, contradictory, or missing key context.
attributes.D2D_Verbatim: Identify if the call mentions anything related to door-to-door (D2D) sales, including phrases such as “an agent knocked on my door,” “someone came to my house,” “I spoke to a salesperson,” “talked to someone at a store,” “a rep came by,” “door-to-door sales,” “signed up at my door,” or “agent visited my home.” If one of these or a close variation appears in the transcript, return the exact phrase or sentence from the transcript where it was mentioned. If no such mention is found, return ."
attributes.do_not_contact: Indicate '1' or '0' whether customer requested to be put on a 'do not call' or 'do not contact' list, or otherwise requested us to stop calling them permanently for Marketing purposes. Do not expand your scope, language must be explicit and specific in context. You are forbidden from considering a one-time request to not call back, requests related to email, requests related to payments, or customers who are leaving the company altogether/saying they'll never choose us.
attributes.do_not_contact_verbatim: If the customer requested to be put on a 'do not call' or 'do not contact' list, or otherwise requested us to stop calling them permanently for Marketing purposes, return verbatim language customer used. Include enough to make sense standalone. You are forbidden from considering a one-time request to not call back, requests related to email, requests related to payments, or customers who are leaving the company altogether/saying they'll never choose us.
attributes.auditory_verbatim:
Identify whether the customer explicitly reports a technical phone/audio issue based only on the transcript.

Return a short exact customer verbatim only when the customer clearly says there is an issue with hearing, audio clarity, or the phone connection.

Count examples only when stated by the customer:
- "I can't hear you"
- "You're cutting out"
- "The line is breaking up"
- "It's hard to hear you"
- "There is static"
- "You sound muffled"
- "Hello? Are you there?"
- "The call dropped" or similar phone/connection issue

Do NOT return anything for:
- "I can't understand you" by itself
- difficulty understanding the agent's accent, pronunciation, wording, pace, or explanation
- confusion about what the agent is asking
- misunderstanding plan details, disclosures, billing, contract language, or account information
- agent statements
- transcript errors or awkward transcription wording

Important:
Because only the transcript is available, do not infer audio problems unless the customer explicitly mentions hearing, audio clarity, static, cutting out, breaking up, silence, or connection trouble.

Output:
- If a technical phone/audio issue is present, return 1 short exact customer quote.
- If not present, return blank.
attributes.web_issue_reasoning: If the customer mentioned a complaint about web performance, or a technical issue with the website, return a short summary here. Must be website, not mobile app. Must be summary from customer POV, not agent. If nothing mentioned, return ''.
attributes.app_issue_reasoning: If the customer mentioned a complaint about app performance, or a technical issue with the app, return a short summary here. Must be mobile app, not website. Must be summary from customer POV, not agent. If nothing mentioned, return ''.

attributes.unauthorized_switch_bo: Did the customer or agent EXPLICITLY mention an unauthorized or unknowing SWITCH in their REP recently? ONLY if so, return '1', otherwise return '0'. Do not return '1' if there are unauthorized changes in anything WITHIN the agent's REP, including administrative errors, rate or plan changes, debt disputes, switch holds, or if no explicit mentions of another REP are made. Consider this return mutually exclusive with 'unauthorized_force_out_bo'.
attributes.igl_candidate_bo:
Determine whether this call has credible Inadvertent Gain/Loss (IGL), Force Out, Rescission, or LOIE/no-power evidence.

Business context:
- Inadvertent Gain: our company mistakenly gained an ESI ID/service address. Examples: wrong address enrolled, customer no longer moving in, third party received our bill, or customer says they never agreed to our service.
- Inadvertent Loss: our customer lost service to another Retail Electric Provider (REP) without authorization. Examples: unexpected final bill, account closed/cancelled, stopped receiving bills, another REP bill/disconnect notice, or customer says they never agreed to switch and wants to stay with us.
- Force Out: same-brand/same-company or same-premise incorrect enrollment where one of our customers may have overwritten another customer. This is not a different-REP unauthorized switch.
- Rescission Gain: customer switched to our company but wants to cancel and return to the previous REP. Rescission applies to switch transactions, not move-ins.
- Rescission Loss: customer switched away from our company to another REP and wants to return.
- LOIE/no power: customer says no power, lights out, disconnected, or urgent service loss.
- Not related: normal billing, payment, plan/rate changes, admin errors, debt disputes, switch holds, same-REP account changes, or unrelated calls.

Return '1' if the call has credible IGL, Force Out, Rescission, LOIE/no-power, or unclear-but-relevant evidence.
Return '0' if the call is unrelated or only involves normal billing/payment/plan/rate/admin/debt/switch-hold/same-REP issues.
attributes.igl_event_type:
Classify the call into exactly one IGL, Force Out, Rescission, LOIE, or non-IGL event type.

Business context:
- Inadvertent Gain: wrong address enrolled, customer no longer moving in, third party received our bill, or customer says they never agreed to our service.
- Inadvertent Loss: customer lost service to another REP without authorization. Examples: unexpected final bill, account closed/cancelled, stopped receiving bills, another REP bill/disconnect notice, or customer says they never agreed to switch and wants to stay with us.
- Force Out: same-brand/same-company or same-premise incorrect enrollment where one customer may have overwritten another customer. This is not a different-REP unauthorized switch.
- Rescission Gain: customer switched to our company but wants to cancel and return to the previous REP. Rescission applies to switch transactions, not move-ins.
- Rescission Loss: customer switched away from our company to another REP and wants to return.
- LOIE/no power: customer says no power, lights out, disconnected, or urgent service loss.
- Not related: normal billing, payment, plan/rate changes, admin errors, debt disputes, switch holds, same-REP account changes, or unrelated calls.

Rules:
Return INADVERTENT_LOSS only when another REP is explicit or strongly implied and the customer denies authorization.
Return RESCISSION_GAIN or RESCISSION_LOSS only when the switch appears authorized or knowingly completed and the customer now wants to reverse it.
Return FORCE_OUT only when same-brand/same-company or same-premise overwrite evidence exists.
Return LOIE_NO_POWER when the customer says no power, lights out, disconnected, or urgent service loss.
Return NO_IGL_RELATED for unrelated calls.
Return UNCLEAR only when there is some IGL/rescission/force-out evidence but not enough to classify.
attributes.igl_expected_action:
Choose the expected agent action under IGL, Force Out, Rescission, and LOIE rules.

Business context:
- Inadvertent Gain usually needs Customer Issue > IGL > IAG case.
- Inadvertent Loss without customer authorization usually needs Customer Issue > IGL > IAL case. Do not submit a new move-in or switch to fix an IGL loss.
- Force Out usually needs Customer Issue > Billing > Force Out case.
- Rescission Gain means the customer switched to our company and wants to return to the prior REP. If eligible, create a Rescission Gain case and explain resolution timing.
- Rescission Loss means the customer switched away from us and wants to return. If the other REP is known and the switch was authorized, advise the customer to contact that REP to request rescission.
- No power/lights out should route to LOIE.
- If the customer knowingly chose another REP or needs normal enrollment help, Customer Success enrollment may be appropriate.
- Normal billing, payment, plan/rate, debt, admin, switch hold, same-REP account changes, or unrelated calls need no IGL action.

Return exactly one expected action.
Return UNCLEAR if the correct action cannot be determined from the transcript.
attributes.igl_agent_risky_action_bo:
Determine whether the agent took or recommended an action that could be risky or incorrect for an IGL, Force Out, Rescission, or LOIE/no-power situation.

Business context:
- For Inadvertent Loss, agents should not submit a new move-in or switch just to regain the customer when the customer did not authorize the other REP.
- For Inadvertent Gain, Force Out, or active IGL resolution, submitting a new move-in, switch, move-out, or transfer of service may break the resolution process or cause a LOIE.
- Force Out should usually route to Customer Issue > Billing > Force Out.
- Rescission Gain should usually route to a Rescission Gain case if eligible.
- Rescission Loss may require advising the customer to contact the other REP to rescind when the other REP is known and the switch was authorized.
- No power/lights out should route to LOIE.
- Telling the customer to contact the TDU/utility for an IGL or unauthorized REP switch is usually incorrect unless the issue is truly an outage/no-power situation.

Return '1' if the agent offered, attempted, recommended, or completed a risky/wrong action such as an inappropriate move-in, switch, move-out, transfer of service, TDU referral, or failure to route LOIE.
Return '0' if no risky action is evident, the call is unrelated, or the agent action is unclear.

Do not return '1' if there are unauthorized changes involving another REP, changes in billing or mailing address, identity theft, OR if the customer was aware, intending to transfer or cancel service. attributes.customer_ror_bo: Did the customer mention an authorized enrollment with a new REP, either by themselves or another household member, that now they want to cancel and return to their previous REP? attributes.competitor_rate_plan: Detail any specific competitor offers mentioned, including plan names and rates. Extract only competitor electricity plans that are explicitly named and include a rate. Always return the competitor name, the plan name, and the exact rate mentioned.
attributes.call_summary_igl: Use a single sentence or two short clauses separated by semicolons that starts with the customer’s name only if explicitly stated in the transcript, identifies the primary issue discussed, states the cause only if the agent explicitly says it, and includes only agent actions that were explicitly stated; do not include customer history or tenure, medical or personal details, emotional language, inferred or added actions, conversation flow summaries, or conclusions, and if a common element is missing explicitly note the absence using neutral language (e.g., “No timeframe was provided,” “Customer was not directed to contact the TDU”), extracting facts only.
attributes.payment_arrangement:
Analyze the customer's conversation to determine if their primary intent is to request an alternative or flexible payment schedule because they cannot meet their current obligation. This intent is indicated if the customer states they cannot pay the full amount, asks for a payment extension, a deferred payment plan, to pay after the due date, proposes breaking the payment into smaller installments, or explains a financial hardship preventing them from paying on time.

If this intent is identified, summarize the customer's situation, including their reason (if provided) and the type of flexibility they are requesting. DO NOT RETURN A summary if the customer is only asking for their balance or due date without expressing any difficulty paying. If this intent is not present, return ".".
attributes.humorous_reasoning: If the call contains hilarity worthy of a sitcom, provide a one or two-sentence reason; otherwise, return ''. The bar is high. Give explicit verbatim details, including customer quotes. Do not count mispronounced or misbranded company names.
attributes.high_bill_flow_4: If a high bill was discussed, indicate '1' or '0' whether the agent made at least one usage recommendation to lower future bills. MIST  BE USAGE RECOMMENDATION, NOT A NEW PLAN. If billing was not discussed on the call,".
attributes.high_bill_flow_3: If a high bill was discussed, indicate ‘1’ or '0' whether the agent provided a personalized review of the customer’s electricity usage by explaining why the customer’s usage is high or variable (e.g., appliances, household behavior, weather, seasonality, or past usage trends specific to the customer). Explaining pricing, rate structure, average price, base charges, delivery charges, or kWh tiers does not qualify even if kWh amounts are mentioned. Otherwise, return ‘ ’.
attributes.high_bill_flow_2: "If a high bill was discussed, indicate ‘1’ or ‘0’ whether the agent actually reviewed the customer’s current plan or recommended a new plan before covering any usage details or making other recommendations. attributes.high_bill_flow_1: If a high bill was discussed, indicate ‘1’ or ‘0’ whether the agent showed genuine empathy and set clear expectations for next steps; assign ‘1’ only when the agent explicitly acknowledges the customer’s feelings with sincere language such as “I understand how frustrating a high bill can be” (or equivalent), Agent MUST restate the problem to count as empathetic, and assign ‘0’ whenever billing is not discussed or the agent’s response sounds dismissive—e.g., merely saying “no worries,” “no problem,” or otherwise failing to convey empathy or set expectations.
attributes.do_not_email: Indicate '1' or '0' whether customer requested to stop being emailed offers or other Marketing/promotion opportunities.

attributes.caller_first_name: Return the caller's first name, or '' if not disclosed.

attributes.directed_to_other_REP_bo: If the agent directed the customer to contact their current or immediately previous REP, especially in relation to switching service or changing providers, mark '1'. If not, or if it never came up, mark '0'.
attributes.cust_callback: Assess as '1' or '0' if customer ended call by explicitly saying they would call back later. Consider verbatim transcript from customer only.
attributes.confidence_level: Rate your confidence in the accuracy of this evaluation as 'High', 'Medium', or 'Low' considering: amount and degree of subjective evaluations, number of suspected transcription errors, and inscrutability of customer responses.

attributes.callback_promised: Assesses whether the agent promised to call the customer back. Return '0' if there is no clear indication that the agent will call the customer back.
attributes.callback_advised: Determine whether the agent instead recommended that the customer call us back. Return '1' if the agent explicitly advises or instructs the customer to call back (e.g., “Give us a call if you need to,” “You can call back later,” etc.). Return '0' if the agent did not advise the customer to call back or if it is unclear.

attributes.customer_confusion:
Task: Classify the customer's confusion level during this interaction.

Use these evidence signals (use what is present in the interaction): stated confusion, number of clarifying questions, examining bill line items, misunderstandings.
Do NOT consider whether the agent assuaged the customer or resolved the issue.

Choose exactly one label:
- Low: minimal or no expressed confusion; few/no clarifying questions; understands the explanation without repeated re-asking.
- Moderate: some expressed confusion or multiple clarifying questions; needs clarification on parts (e.g., specific bill line items) but shows partial understanding.
- High: repeated or strong expressed confusion; frequent/repetitive clarifying questions; persistent misunderstandings even after explanations.

Output format: Return exactly one of: Low, Moderate, High. Return only the single word.
attributes.customer_sentiment_start: Define the customer's beginning sentiment as either 'Positive', 'Negative', or 'Neutral'. You should limit 'Neutral' and skew toward either 'Positive' or 'Negative' whenever possible.
attributes.customer_sentiment_end: Define the customer's concluding sentiment as either 'Positive', 'Negative', or 'Neutral'. You should limit 'Neutral' and skew toward either 'Positive' or 'Negative' whenever possible.
attributes.customer_satisfaction: Rate the customer's overall satisfaction level as 'Satisfied', 'Dissatisfied', or 'Neutral' based on their words and inferred tone. Lean toward 'Dissatisfied' over 'Neutral'. Receiving a resolution does not guarantee 'Satisfied' if the rest of the experience was poor. A successful sale should lean toward 'Satisfied' over 'Neutral' unless high customer effort was required. Any negative mentions of agent accent or understandability should skew toward 'Dissatisfied'.
attributes.customer_satisfaction_reasoning: Return a succinct summary of why the customer's final satisfaction level was either 'Satisfied', 'Dissatisfied', or 'Neutral. Maximize brevity.
attributes.callback_risk: Indicate how likely you deem the customer to call back in the next 7-10 days -- due to a pending issue, or another reason you discern -- as 'Very Unlikely', 'Unlikely', 'Neutral', 'Likely', or 'Very Likely'. Moderate confusion on a topic is unlikely to create a callback, must be severe. Once an account is successfully cancelled, it is exceedingly rare for the customer to call back for any reason, including a future move-in. Customers who successfully change their plan rarely call back either. Customers who threaten to leave and change providers aren't likely to call back.
attributes.callback_predicted: Give short rationale for your chosen evaluation of callback_risk.
attributes.non_commodity_offer: List the names of any non-electricity products offered, correcting any transcription errors within context of home warranty or green energy. If none, ''.
attributes.customer_insult_verbatim: If the customer personally insulted the agent or the company, return short verbatim details here.

attributes.website_save_tips:
Task:
Determine whether the agent directed the customer to the company's energy-saving tips website or online energy-saving resources as a way to reduce or understand future energy costs.

Return exactly one of these:
"1"
"0"
""

Rules:
• Only evaluate agent statements from the current call.
• Return "1" if the call is about a high bill, bill increase, or usage concern AND the agent directs the customer to an energy-saving tips website, online saving tips page, usage/savings tools, or similar company online resource.

attributes.trusted_advisor_reasoning:
Analyze the call transcript for evidence that the agent created a **customer-focused interaction** by using these skills:

- **Flexing Communication** (matching pace/detail/tone to the customer’s style: Driver, Amiable, Expressive, Analytic)
- **Conveying Advocacy** (empathetic support + transparency/ownership so the customer feels supported/assured/worry-free)
- **Active Listening** (clarifying questions, paraphrasing/confirming understanding, patient/judgment-free engagement)
- **Surfacing Additional Information** (open-ended questions/purposeful small talk to uncover helpful context)
- **Acknowledging Baggage** (recognizing prior unresolved issues/repeat contacts/impact, acknowledging it, then moving forward positively)
- **Using Positive Language** (constructive phrasing like “What I can do…”, “Let’s take a look…”, “I recommend…”, avoiding “I can’t/No/Policy…”)
- **Positioning Alternatives** (offering options aligned to surfaced needs when the initial request isn’t available)
- **Recognizing Opportunities** (proactively preventing likely future contacts without overwhelming the customer)
- **Connecting the Dots** (explaining why a proactive point matters and how it connects to the customer’s situation)

### Output rules (strict)

- If **none** of the skills above are clearly evidenced, return exactly: `""`
- If **any** are evidenced, return a **2–3 sentence** justification that:
  - **Names at least 2 specific skills** from the list above (include **Using Positive Language** if it is present)
  - Includes **1–3 brief quoted phrases OR clearly labeled paraphrases** from the transcript as evidence (no speculation)
  - Is **customer-outcome oriented** (supported/assured/worry-free, clarified understanding, added value beyond the basic need)

### Evidence requirement

Only count a skill if the transcript contains explicit language/behavior consistent with it. Do not infer intent.

attributes.excessive_talk_reasoning:
If the agent spoke at length in a non-excluded section of the call, identify the reason for the agent’s excessive talk.

Return a brief one-sentence explanation only when the excessive talk occurred outside of required disclosure, TPV, contract, authorization, or enrollment language.

The reason must include the approximate timestamp or timestamp range where the non-excluded excessive talk occurred.

Excessive talk means:
- the agent spoke for more than 200 consecutive words without a meaningful customer interruption, or
- the agent spoke at length while the customer only gave short acknowledgments such as “okay,” “yes,” “mhmm,” “correct,” or similar responses.

A meaningful customer interruption means the customer asks a question, gives new information, objects, redirects the conversation, or meaningfully participates in the discussion.

Do NOT return a reason if the long agent speech occurred during required or official language, including:
- TPV language
- official sales terms
- disclosures
- contract reads
- authorization reads
- enrollment authorization
- plan terms and conditions
- required enrollment confirmations
- required yes/no verification questions
- rate, base charge, TDU charge, early cancellation fee, or plan charge disclosures when part of the required enrollment read
- paperless billing authorization language
- service start date, service address, or account setup confirmations when part of the required enrollment process

Do not use excluded sections as the reason for excessive talk, even if the agent spoke for a long time during those sections.

Return a reason only when the long agent speech occurs outside required disclosure or authorization language, such as:
- a sales pitch
- an upsell pitch
- repeated persuasion after customer confusion or hesitation
- unnecessary explanation
- off-topic monologue
- long product explanation outside of required enrollment language
- agent commentary that prevents the customer from speaking

If the only long agent speech occurred during TPV, disclosures, contract reads, authorization language, official sales terms, or required enrollment confirmations, return "".

If there is no clear non-excluded excessive talk, return "".

Examples of valid outputs:
"At 09:30:55-09:34:12, the agent spoke at length while repeatedly explaining the optional Green App upsell after the customer expressed confusion."
"At 09:51:22-09:52:55, the agent gave a long non-required explanation about additional account options without a meaningful customer interruption."
"At approximately 09:53:40, the agent continued pitching an optional product after the customer appeared hesitant."

- The agent read the contract authorization.
- The agent read plan terms and conditions.
- The agent read required enrollment disclosures.
- The agent asked required yes/no authorization questions.
- The agent confirmed service start date, address, or account setup as part of enrollment.

Use only the current call transcript.
Must review the verbatim transcript and apply the exclusions before returning a reason.
Return only the one-sentence reason with timestamp, or "".

attributes.preferred_term: Did the customer verbalize preference for longer term length, shorter term length, or neither?
attributes.hvac_owned: Identify type and number of heaters/air conditioners customer mentions owning or using (e.g., two central A/C, three electric space heaters), or else ''.
attributes.move_reconsideration:
This needs to be the final field evaluated, and should be independent from any other context.
If moving, judge the customer’s hypothetical likelihood to select the company again in the undefined future after they finish with their new provider as ‘Unlikely’, ‘Likely’, or ‘Neutral’.
If explicit mentions of reconsideration occur, mark ‘Likely’; otherwise, evaluate based on satisfaction and ease of interaction.
An easy process without dissatisfaction increases likelihood, regardless of moving in or out of state.
Return only ‘Likely’, ‘Unlikely’, or ‘Neutral’.
If moving_soon is ‘0’ or tos_closed is ‘1’, return blank.
attributes.move_reconsideration_reasoning: Provide a one-sentence reason for your evaluation of move reconsideration.
attributes.smart_thermostat: Identify whether the customer mentions having a smart thermostat at the discussed location. Return '1' if the customer explicitly says they have a smart thermostat at the discussed location. Return '0' if smart thermostat ownership at the discussed location is explicitly discussed and the customer indicates they do not have one there. Exclude mentions relating to any other location. Return blank if smart thermostat ownership at the discussed location is not mentioned or cannot be determined from the conversation. Output only the result.
attributes.thermostat_setting: If customer disclosed the temperature they set their thermostat too, return here. Otherwise, return ''.
attributes.plan_awareness: If the customer wanted a specific plan or offer from us, categorize how they heard of it as one of the following: 'In-Store', 'Online', 'Friends/family', 'Mail', 'Email', 'Advertisement', 'Door-to-door', 'Social Media', or 'Other'. If they are speaking about a competitor's plan, or if there is no customer mention of a plan, return ''.
attributes.plan_request_by_name: Indicate '1' or '0' whether the customer requested a specific plan by name.
attributes.happy_occasion: If the customer mentioned any happy and notable life events, such as getting married, having a baby, etc., return a summary here. Must be personal to the customer, and customer MUST indicate it is a happy occasion to qualify. Do not consider any events related to negative circumstances.
attributes.price_sensitivity: Rate the customer's sensitivity to price as 'High', 'Moderate', or 'Low'. If no rates or plans were discussed, ''.
attributes.same_plan_expected: On renewals only, indicate '1' or '0' whether the customer has distinct impression of renewing on the exact same plan or the same rate. If customer understands that the plan name or benefits are the same, but the rate is different, mark '0'.

attributes.defection_risk: Assess concluding likelihood of customer canceling their current account as 'Very High', 'High', 'Moderate', 'Low', or 'Very Low'. All move-outs or cancelations due to circumstance or situation should be 'Very High', unless move-out is accompanied by transferring service. Customer being intensely focused on their plan or rate, or customer asking about cancel fees, are all 'Very High' regardless of satisfaction. When plans or competitors were discussed, must end in a sale or else it is 'High' or 'Very High'. Ending the call unsatisfied with high bill or usage is 'High' or 'Very High'. Copies of bills could be 'Moderate' or 'High' depending on context. Difficulty paying is not in and of itself a high defection risk because there are flexible payment options available. Lack of definitive or explicit intent to cancel are not valid evaluation criteria. Consider actual transcript verbatim comments.
attributes.defection_risk_reasoning: Provide a one-sentence reason for your evaluation of the defection risk. All of the following is context. All move-outs or cancelations due to circumstance or situation should be 'Very High', unless move-out is accompanied by transferring service. Customer being intensely focused on their plan or rate, or customer asking about cancel fees, are all 'Very High' regardless of satisfaction. When plans or competitors were discussed, must end in a sale or else it is 'High' or 'Very High'. Ending the call unsatisfied with high bill or usage is 'High' or 'Very High'. Copies of bills could be 'Moderate' or 'High' depending on context. Difficulty paying is not in and of itself a high defection risk because there are flexible payment options available. All other scenarios require your best judgment. Lack of definitive or explicit intent to cancel are not valid evaluation criteria. Consider actual transcript verbatim comments.
attributes.future_info: Include succinct information divulged by customer that would help future customer service or sales, or tells us about their lifestyle or home characteristics. Shopping preferences and favored plan features must be included. Exclude price sensitivity, and traditional account or CRM data such as tenure, etc. Return data points only.
